If you're not strong-willed, I wouldn't recommend this place.
This dental clinic was recommended by a friend who said they accept the government's universal healthcare scheme. It's located near King Kaew Market on Bang Na-Trat Road. The clinic is clean and the service is good. They accept the universal healthcare scheme. I intended to use my universal healthcare scheme for a teeth cleaning (tartar removal). The dentist said it required root planing and would cost around 10,000 baht, so I didn't do it. Since I was already there, I told the dentist I felt I had a cavity and wanted a filling, using my universal healthcare scheme. As the procedure progressed, the dentist kept saying I had more cavities and the cost kept increasing, eventually totaling about 17 cavities and costing 15,900 baht (the dentist said that wasn't the final price). During the procedure, as more cavities appeared, I kept asking the dentist if the cavities were definitely decayed and if there were any rotting parts. The dentist kept stating the costs, but I was too soft-hearted.

After that, I went to another clinic. The dentist there said a teeth cleaning without root planing was possible. The dentist also said that, judging from my teeth, I didn't seem to have that many cavities, and that the fillings I had done earlier weren't necessary. It looks like it might be a dental filling.
Summary:
*The clinic is reasonably clean.
**The dentist gave advice throughout, but shouldn't be too pushy with sales pitches.
***If you're not strong-willed, I don't recommend going here. The budget will spiral out of control. I went for a free teeth cleaning using my government health insurance, but came home confused, wondering how I ended up paying 15,900 baht.
